correctness.rationale: The edge signature is exactly the Hamming disagreement count outside the edge direction. A complete mask-based \((d-1)\)- and \(d\)-subset scan and a separately implemented breadth-first-search distance-vector scan agree on all four joint minima and all basis sets for dimensions \(2\) through \(5\); both directly verify the finite geometric families, with \(176\) and \(160\) optima in the two nontrivial cases. Exhaustion and monotonicity rule out all smaller joint sets. For dimensions four and five, ordinary edge-resolution also fails at sizes two and three, respectively. Computations are exact and replayed from the delivered source files.

value.rationale: The 2022 composite invariant asks for joint distance identification and local edge coverage, a natural dual requirement in graph sensor design. The small binary cubes are canonical Cartesian powers, and these are the first dimensions in the tested sequence where edge resolution alone is insufficient: the cardinality must increase by exactly one. Exhaustive geometric classification discovers three separate optimizer orbits in the four-cube and only one in the five-cube, a useful sharp finite benchmark and boundary for further cube research. No general higher-dimensional result is claimed.
